links.outcome: Hallucinated or ungrounded clinical content in LLM-generated diabetes meal plans
links.effect: Frequent hallucinations and lack of clinical contextualization were noted across the three LLMs; RAG integration was identified as a potential improvement but was not tested.
links.quote: Frequent hallucinations and lack of clinical contextualization were noted.

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM dietary plans with T2DM guidelines and the nutrition care process
links.effect: None of the models fully matched the NCP framework, particularly diagnosis and monitoring. Energy alignment was 70.9% for ChatGPT-4.1 and 83.1% for Grok-3. There were fat overestimation, micronutrient shortfalls, and carbohydrate underdelivery.
links.quote: None of the models demonstrated full concordance with the NCP framework, particularly in the diagnosis and monitoring components.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy, safety, and guideline adherence of three LLMs in generating meal plans for simulated type 2 diabetes profiles without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
